title: Web-based cryptography is always snake oil
summary: This article argues that web-based cryptography implemented in JavaScript is fundamentally insecure and unreliable. The core issue is that any server-side attacker can modify the JavaScript code before it reaches the browser, completely undermining the cryptographic protection. The author explains why browser-based cryptography cannot provide true security guarantees, as the execution environment itself is controlled by potentially malicious code.
problem_solved: Explains why browser-based cryptography is inherently flawed and cannot replace server-side cryptographic operations.
why_valuable: Raises critical security awareness about the fundamental trust problem in client-side cryptographic implementations, helping developers avoid dangerous misconceptions.
